name: InventoryMenu_DrawAbilityListPage
domain: Draws one page (up to five rows) of an owner's abilities inside the inventory-menu subsystem, alongside a header for the owner currently open in the menu.
expressed: dereferences the global InventoryMenuState pointer (Data_03001f2c) and resolves the owner object for menu->item_owner via Runtime_GetObject/OwnerState_GetFar (Func_08077008)

commits the window, then computes first_entry = state->page*5 and visible_count = min(state->entry_count-first_entry, 5), matching InventoryMenu_DrawItemNamePage's (Func_080a56c8) established page-math idiom

draws the scrollbar/page furniture via Func_080a2324(5, first_entry, window, 80, 58) and Menu_DrawPageIndicator(window, state->entry_count, 5, state->page, 28), then a fixed header string (message 0xAED) at (176,0)

loops over up to 5 entries of menu->items[] starting at first_entry: for each entry, looks up Ability_GetData(item & 0x3fff) and draws the entry's name/message text at x=88 and its icon (ability[9]) at x=176, both at y = row*16+16

computes a per-entry count/level value from ability[8] (0xff sentinel maps to 11, otherwise ability[8]-1) and draws it via Func_080a8cc0 (a tile-based two/three-glyph number widget already exact-adopted at this address) at tile position (25, row*2+2)
after the loop, if menu->item_count == 0 draws an 'empty' message (0xAEF) at (96,17)

draws the current owner's portrait (Func_08015090), a name/class message built from owner+0x129 plus message-table base Value_00000741, a fixed glyph at ROM address 0x080AF22C (immediately adjacent to InventoryMenu_DrawStatDelta's IncreaseGlyph/DecreaseGlyph at 0x080AF224/0x080AF228), and the owner's level-like byte at owner+15 via UiNumber_DrawAt
always returns 1, matching the InventoryMenu_Draw*Page callback convention

bounded_search.reason: candidate now matches the reference's 380-byte extent exactly; 28 differing halfwords / 38 wrong instructions remain, concentrated in a few register-allocation/scheduling hunks, outside the <=20-halfword admission gate.

notes: The family-matcher's best guess, games/gs1/src/menu/select_quantity.c (score 7245/10000, below the 7500 confidence threshold), shares only the register-shuffle prologue idiom common to every owner in this size class; it does not share Data_03001f2c's InventoryMenuState typing, any callee, or any field offset with this owner and was treated as a false positive per this session's prior findings about the highest-scoring cluster.

Real family evidence instead comes from hand-tracing games/gs1/asm/080a8f40.s directly and following its call targets into already-adopted inventory_menu/ sources: Data_03001f2c dereferences to the exact same InventoryMenuState* used by games/gs1/src/inventory_menu/draw_item_name_page.c (Func_080a56c8, aliased InventoryMenu_DrawItemNamePage), which shares this owner's exact (window, unused, const struct MenuResult*) signature, its Func_080a2324/Menu_DrawPageIndicator call shape, and its first_entry=page*5 / visible_count=min(entry_count-first_entry,5) page math verbatim.

menu->item_owner (struct field offset 0x21a) and menu->item_count (0x218) match inventory_menu.h's InventoryMenuState exactly. The owner lookup Func_08077008 is the veneer already declared in owner_state.h as OwnerState_GetFar/Runtime_GetObject, used identically (Runtime_GetObject(menu->item_owner)) in the already-adopted games/gs1/src/inventory_menu/draw_selected_item_header.c.

The per-row lookup Func_08077080 is the veneer already aliased project-wide in types.h as Ability_GetData (also BattleAction_Get in battle_runtime.h -- same address, two subsystem views). Its target Func_08078b9c is already exact-adopted at games/gs1/src/battle/get_action_definition.c (BattleAction_GetDirect), which masks its argument with the identical 0x3fff constant seen at this owner's two ldrh sites, and games/gs1/src/psynergy_menu/classify_selected_psynergy.c independently corroborates both the 0x3fff mask AND the ability[8]==0xff sentinel check on the exact same Ability_GetData return value, from an unrelated subsystem call site -- strong convergent evidence this really is the Ability/BattleAction data pointer, not a coincidental match.

The fixed glyph pool constant 0x080AF22C sits exactly 4/8 bytes past games/gs1/src/inventory_menu/draw_stat_delta.c's InventoryMenu_IncreaseGlyph (0x080AF224) and InventoryMenu_DecreaseGlyph (0x080AF228) -- the same small glyph-sheet ROM blob, reinforcing the inventory_menu subsystem placement.

menu->items[] (u16 array at struct offset 0x1c8) is read here as a raw ability/action id feed rather than a plain item id; the field's existing name from inventory_menu.h is kept as-is per this project's low-confidence-naming rule -- this owner does not rename or reinterpret that field, it only records that its runtime contents are consumed as Ability_GetData() input in this particular page.

2026-08-27, structural workbench + iterative fixes (games/gs1/asm/080a8f40.s traced by hand first; m2c's output via `compiler workbench` used only as a starting hypothesis and independently corroborated the same struct fields/constants/masks derived from the manual trace): the initial draft (menu pointer dereferenced early, item array walked via a separately incremented u16* rather than menu-relative offset arithmetic) scored 87.7% objdiff / 141 differing halfwords with the reference keeping `menu` permanently in fp across the whole function while the draft spilled it to the stack. Rewriting the loop to re-index through `menu` via a raw byte offset accumulator (matching this project's existing LoadByte-style idiom for fields beyond a struct's modeled boundary) let `menu` live in fp for the whole function again and cut the diff to 107 halfwords / 376 candidate bytes (4 short). The single largest remaining fix was branch-body order in the per-row count computation: writing `if (ability[8] == 0xff) count = 11; else count = ability[8]-1;` (matching the reference's actual bne/fallthrough shape) rather than the equivalent `!=`-first phrasing dropped differing halfwords from 107 to 28 and brought candidate_bytes to the exact 380-byte reference extent in one step -- both phrasings are logically identical but this compiler speculatively hoists whichever branch is written first when the other is a bare read-and-subtract, and only the '==0xff -> 11' first ordering matches the reference's un-hoisted branch/fallthrough/jump structure.

Residual (28 differing halfwords / 38 wrong instructions, all register-allocation/scheduling, no remaining algorithm or call-argument-value mismatch): (1) the two per-row ldrh+ands sequences for the masked item id consistently put the loaded halfword in r0 and the 0x3fff literal in r3 in this draft, versus item-in-r3/mask-in-r0 in the reference -- the final `ands r0,r3` instruction itself is byte-identical either way, only the preceding load's destination register differs; tried both `item & 0x3fff` and `0x3fff & item` operand order with no effect. (2) the count-computation branch, while now correctly un-hoisted for the `==0xff` case, still hoists `ability[8]-1` into r4 before the compare (reference computes it only in the taken branch, reusing the already-loaded r4 rather than reloading r3); introducing a named `u8 uses = ability[8]` local to force a single load regressed candidate size back to 376 bytes, so it was reverted. (3) two 5-argument calls (the icon draw at ability[9]/176/y and the closing UiNumber_DrawAt at owner+15) build their register file in a different order than the reference despite identical left-to-right C argument lists; splitting either argument into its own named local made no measurable difference and was reverted in favor of the more legible direct form. None of these were forced with asm(), register hints, or PERM_GENERAL-style pinning, per project rules -- they are left as an honest residual for a future pass.
